title: analogWrite and PWM: brightness and speed from a digital pin

spans.text: PWM rapidly switches a digital output to control average power, which can dim an LED or control a suitable DC motor. On classic UNO, `analogWrite` usually produces PWM with a 0–255 duty range, not a true analog voltage. ESP32 configures PWM through its LEDC peripheral/API.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Use a pin that supports PWM and check each board's frequency and resolution rules. Do not power a motor from GPIO; use a driver and suitable external supply.
